look_here_first: Look at spacing along the spike: flowers and broad bracts are visibly separated along a long slender, often nodding or drooping rachis rather than packed into a dense head.

project_inclusion.range_basis: USDA-derived county native-status data explicitly marks Bell, Burnet and Comal native; additional qualifying counties include Gillespie, Kerr, San Saba, Travis and Williamson.

best_field_traits: narrow linear to narrowly oblong gland-dotted leaflets
long slender terminal spike with visibly separated flowers and bracts
broad conspicuous bracts along an obvious rachis
nine stamens as a technical confirmation
morphology_keys.habit: Herbaceous perennial with one to a few stems, branching above.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Odd-pinnate; narrow linear to narrowly oblong leaflets, gland-dotted beneath.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Long slender loose terminal spike, often nodding/drooping.
morphology_keys.flower: Sessile or nearly sessile flowers visibly spaced along rachis.
morphology_keys.reproductive_detail: Nine stamens provide a technical confirmation.

comparisons.key_distinctions: D. compacta and D. purpurea pack flowers into dense spikes/heads; D. aurea is densely silky. D. enneandra exposes much more rachis between flowers/bracts.
